drills.title: Same shapes, different data
drills.code:
f = jax.jit(loss)
f(params, x, y)          # batch 0, int32[32,128]
f(params, x_next, y_next) # batch 1, same shapes
drills.why: The cache key is shapes, dtypes, the pytree structure and static values, never the numbers. New data with the same signature reuses the executable.

drills.title: A smaller last batch
drills.code:
f(params, x, y)            # int32[32,128]
f(params, x[:16], y[:16])  # int32[16,128]: the ragged last batch
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  different input types:
  * at x, now i32[16,128] and before i32[32,128]
  * at y, now i32[16,128] and before i32[32,128]
drills.why: A new shape is a new program: XLA compiles for exact shapes. The usual fix is to drop the last batch or pad it to the full size and mask the padding out of the loss.

drills.title: Back to a shape seen before
drills.code:
f(params, x, y)            # [32,128]: compile 1
f(params, x[:16], y[:16])  # [16,128]: compile 2
f(params, x, y)            # [32,128] again
drills.why: Every signature stays in the cache for the life of the jitted function, so alternating between two shapes compiles twice in total, not on every switch.

drills.title: Variable sequence length
drills.code:
f(params, x, y)                  # [32,128]
for T in (64, 96, 112, 128):     # real text arrives in many lengths
    f(params, x[:, :T], y[:, :T])
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  different input types:
  * at x, now i32[32,64] and before i32[32,128]
  * at y, now i32[32,64] and before i32[32,128]
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  different input types:
  * at x, now i32[32,96] and before i32[32,128]
  * at y, now i32[32,96] and before i32[32,128]
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  different input types:
  * at x, now i32[32,112] and before i32[32,128]
  * at y, now i32[32,112] and before i32[32,128]
drills.why: Three new lengths, three compiles (128 was cached). With free-form lengths this becomes a recompilation storm; production code pads to a few bucket sizes (for example powers of two) so the number of programs is bounded.

drills.title: A NumPy array instead of a JAX array
drills.code:
f(params, x, y)                  # jax.Array int32[32,128]
f(params, np.asarray(x), np.asarray(y))  # numpy int32[32,128]
drills.why: The abstract value is the same (int32[32,128]); jit copies the NumPy array to the device and reuses the executable.

drills.title: NumPy int64 input
drills.code:
f(params, x, y)                  # int32
f(params, x.astype(np.int64), y.astype(np.int64))
drills.why: With 64-bit mode off (the default, jax_enable_x64=False) JAX canonicalises int64 to int32 before building the key, so this hits the cache. Turn x64 on and it would be a new program.

drills.title: A Python float that changes
drills.code:
f(params, x, y, 1.0)
f(params, x, y, 0.5)   # scale is an ordinary (traced) argument
drills.why: A Python scalar passed as a normal argument becomes a traced weakly typed float32[] (shown as ~float32[]); its value is data, not part of the key.

drills.title: The same float, marked static
drills.code:
fs = jax.jit(loss, static_argnames='scale')
fs(params, x, y, scale=1.0)
for s in (0.5, 0.25, 1.0):
    fs(params, x, y, scale=s)
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  cache miss explanation unavailable
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  cache miss explanation unavailable
drills.why: A static argument's Python value is baked into the program, so each new value compiles (0.5 and 0.25), and a value seen before (1.0) is a hit. Make an argument static only when it changes the program's structure (a flag, a layer count, a shape), never for a value that varies each step such as a learning rate.

drills.title: A Python 2.0 against jnp.float32(2.0)
drills.code:
f(params, x, y, 2.0)              # Python float: weakly typed ~float32[]
f(params, x, y, jnp.float32(2.0))  # a strongly typed float32[] array
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  different input types:
  * at scale, now f32[]{weak_type=False} and before f32[]{weak_type=True}https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/type_promotion.html#weak-types
drills.why: Same value, same shape, same dtype, but weak typing is part of the abstract value: a Python scalar is ~float32[] (it defers to the other operand's dtype in arithmetic), a jnp scalar is float32[]. The cache-miss log says exactly that.

drills.title: One more entry in the parameter dict
drills.code:
f(params, x, y)
f({**params, 'extra': jnp.zeros(())}, x, y)   # unused by the model
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  for loss defined at run_recompile.py
  all previously seen cache keys differ. For the closest previous key:
  different input pytree:
  * at input path [0][0], now <class 'dict'> with 6 children and before <class 'dict'> with 5 children, so the numbers of children do not match, with the symmetric difference of key sets: {'extra'}
drills.why: The pytree structure (the tree definition: keys, nesting, number of leaves) is part of the key, even if the new leaf is never used.

drills.title: jax.jit called inside the loop
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  never seen function:
    <lambda> defined at run_recompile.py
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  never seen function:
    <lambda> defined at run_recompile.py
  but seen another function defined on the same line; maybe the function is
  being re-defined repeatedly, preventing caching?
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  never seen function:
    <lambda> defined at run_recompile.py
  but seen another function defined on the same line; maybe the function is
  being re-defined repeatedly, preventing caching?
drills.why: The trace cache is keyed on the Python function object; a new lambda each iteration is a function never seen before, so every step traces, lowers and compiles again (measured: 3 traces and 3 XLA compiles for 3 steps), even though the program is identical each time. JAX's own log even guesses the cause: "maybe the function is being re-defined repeatedly". Jit once, outside the loop.

drills.title: jax.jit(loss) re-wrapped every step, same function
drills.code:
for step in range(3):
    jax.jit(loss)(params, x, y)   # a new jit wrapper, the same loss function
drills.explain:
TRACING CACHE MISS at the call site:
  never seen function:
    loss defined at run_recompile.py
drills.why: One trace and one compile for three steps (measured). The trace cache is keyed on the underlying Python function, not on the jit wrapper, so re-wrapping the same function hits the cache; it is the new lambda per step (the drill above) that defeats it. Still, jit once outside the loop: it is clearer and skips the wrapper overhead.

drills.title: A global changed between calls
drills.code:
SCALE = 1.0
fg = jax.jit(lambda p, x: apply(p, x).mean() * SCALE)
fg(params, x)    # traced with SCALE = 1.0
SCALE = 100.0
fg(params, x)    # what does it return?
drills.why: No recompile, and a stale answer: the global was read once, while tracing, and baked into the program as a constant. The second call returns exactly the first value, not 100 times it. Pass anything that changes as an argument.

note: Counted on Apple M1 Pro (CPU) with jax 0.11.2; counts are deterministic, independent of the machine.
